Welcome to Springfield Infant School and Nursery
Welcome to Springfield Infants School and Nursery. We are proud of our happy, friendly school and delighted that you would like to find out more about us. We believe that Springfield is a special place for children to begin their learning journey.
Every child in our school is a valued individual. We strive to create opportunities for all to live our values every day and for every member of our school family to be Inclusive, Creative, Ambitious and Nurturing.
Our fantastic staff team are committed to ensuring that every child gets the best possible start to their education, knowing that strong foundations are what future success is built upon.
We have a robust safeguarding ethos, promoting the well-being and welfare of all the children in our care. We understand that feeling safe and happy in school creates a positive learning environment.
As headteacher, it is my pleasure to welcome you to Springfield. We hope you are excited to find out more about us and everything we have to offer, thank you for visiting!
Clare Mavin, Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Common rules about illness absences - Springfield Infant School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
Common rules about illness absences
Minor illness
If your child is unwell on a school day, please always contact the school office before 9.15am.
Please click on the NHS link for more information on childhood illnesses and time off from school
NHS- Is My Child Too Ill For School? Visit page
Longer-term absence
If your child is absent from school for three or more days, or is often absent for short spells, the Head Teacher may ask you to present a doctor’s note to verify the reason for absence. A letter from a parent or carer is needed when:
In cases of further concern, staff, parents and carers can ask for the advice of the school nursing team.
Your contact details
Please make sure that the school office has your up-to-date contact details. It is vitally important that school staff can contact you during the day if your child is not well enough to stay in school.
Our contact details
School Secretary – Miss Amy CarpenterSchool Office (01903) 219243School Email office@springfieldschool.co.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Eco-Warriors - Springfield Infant School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
Eco-Warriors
Springfield was very privileged to be selected as West Sussex County Council recycling heroes!
Everything is collected in classroom bins and recycled through ‘Recycling in Lancing’ to raise money for local charities.
Paper towels and shredded paper also end up in the outdoor compost piles, and before they know it can be used to grow vegetables in the school community garden.
With the help of teacher and Eco Lead Mrs Enticott and Miss Pernet, the children learn in their 3 Rs classes about the importance of Reducing, Reusing and Recycling, and have done so well, that they beat over 200 schools to come second in a community education competition.
All hail the eco warriors of Springfield Infant School in Sackville Road!
Check out our video below!!

pageCache.pageTitle: Music Lessons  - Springfield Infant School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
Music Lessons
We encourage children to learn a musical instrument and we are happy for them to take lessons in school during the day.
Piano and Violin Lessons
Our piano and violin teacher will be Emily Wylie. Emily is an experienced music teacher in the area and has worked at various schools and teaches children of all ages and abilities. She is an accomplished pianist and violinist with 21 years teaching experience. Emily will teach the children to play as well as to read music, aural training and performance pieces.
If you would like your child to begin piano and violin lessons you can contact Emily by email: emilywylie.music@outlook.com or 07769158865
Lessons for Reception aged children run for 20 minutes and are £12 per lesson. Children in years 1 & 2 will have 30 minute lessons at £18 payable in advance, half termly.
Piano and Violin Lessons Flyer Download (pdf)
Guitar Lessons
Max Gasson teaches guitar lessons to children on a Friday morning in school. Max is a qualified teacher offering individual and group sessions. Max will teach your child how to play the guitar, read music and how to perform as part of a group!
If you would like to book with Max email maxgassonmusic@outlook.com with your child’s name, school and year group.
Lessons are £9 for a 30 minute weekly group lesson and £20 for an individual 30 minute lesson, to be paid upfront in a block at the start of the half term. Lessons are open to all year groups. Guitars are provided by Max.
Guitar Lesson Flyer Download (pdf)
Other Instruments
The West Sussex Music Service offers tuition for children and young people in a range of instruments or voice – most tuition takes place at school during term time. If you are interested please contact West Sussex Music:
West Sussex Music Visit website
Head OfficeWest Sussex MusicHerbert Shiner SchoolSouth GrovePetworthWest Sussex, GU28 0EETel: 08452 082 182 or 01798 343 361
Email: music@westsussexmusic.co.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: National Tutoring and Recovery  - Springfield Infant School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
National Tutoring and Recovery
The National Tutoring Programme (NTP) provides schools with funding to spend on targeted academic support, delivered by trained experienced teachers.
The Recovery Premium Grant is part of the government’s package of funding to support pupils whose education has been impacted by coronavirus (COVID-19). It is focused on pupil premium eligible pupils, however, schools can use it to deliver evidence-based approaches for supporting any pupil based on an assessment of individual need.

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast Club - Springfield Infant School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club
Our not-for-profit Breakfast Club is open to all Springfield children, five mornings a week during term time. Children will receive a nutritious breakfast and participate in some fun physical and creative activities that will set them up for a productive day in the classroom. There is no need to book in advance, you can just turn up on the day.
Breakfast Club Registration Form Download (doc)
Open from 8am
All year groups welcome
Working? You could get financial help
If you are working, you may be eligible to get financial help to pay for breakfast club sessions. With a tax-free childcare account, the government will pay in £2 for every £8 you add to your account. So, for example, if you paid in £35 (2 weeks sessions in the breakfast club), the government would also pay in £7 (so the equivalent of 2 SESSIONS FREE). It is very simple to see if you are eligible and to create an account to enable you to pay us for sessions. Simply visit the below website and follow the step-by-step instructions:
https://www.gov.uk/get-tax-free-childcare Visit website

pageCache.pageTitle: Phonics, spelling and reading - Springfield Infant School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
Phonics, spelling and reading
Springfield Infant School places a great emphasis on children’s acquisition of basic skills, including phonics and reading skills. The school uses the Read Write Inc Phonic programme in Nursery, Reception and Year 1. By Year 2 most children are ready to begin the Read Write Inc Spelling programme. Both of these programmes match the 2014 National Curriculum.
Learning to read is one the most important things your child will learn at our school. We want your child to leave Springfield as a competent reader, but we also work to inspire a love of books that will help children develop their skills by reading for pleasure.
How will my child be taught to read?
We start by teaching phonics to the children in Reception. (Phonics is also introduced to our Nursery children during the Summer term). This means that they learn how to ‘read’ the sounds in words and how those sounds can be written down. This is essential for reading, but it also helps children learn to spell well.
The children also practise reading (and spelling) what we call red words (tricky words), such as ‘once,’ ‘have,’ ‘said’ and ‘where’.
The teachers read to the children, too, so that the children get to know all sorts of stories, poetry and information books. They learn many more words this way and it helps their writing.
What is Read Write Inc Phonics?
Read Write Inc is a systematic phonics program that teaches all children to read. For most children it lasts for two years if they start to learn to read in Reception. It teaches the sounds first, in a specific order, and then teaches children how to blend those sounds together in order to read real words.
Please follow this links below for more detailed information on Read Write Inc Phonics:
RWI Presentation Download (pdf)
Letter Formation Ditties Download (pdf)
Parents Reading Information Download (pdf)
How will I know how well my child is doing?
We will always let you know how well your child is doing. We use various ways to find out how the children are progressing with their reading. We use this information to decide what level books they should be reading and what phonics group they should be in. Your child will work with children who are at the same reading level as them and children will move to a different group if they are making faster progress than the others. Your child will have one-to-one support if we think he or she needs some extra help to keep up.
In the summer term, the government asks us to do a phonics check with all the Year 1 children. That gives us extra information about their progress. We will talk to you about how well your child has done, and especially if we have any worries at all.
How long will it take to learn to read well?
By the end of Year 2, your child should be able to read aloud books that are at the right level for his or her age.
What can I do to help? Is there anything that I shouldn’t do?
We provide regular workshops to explain how we teach reading. Please come and support your child.
We would very much like you to know how to help your child to sound out the letters in words and then to ‘push’ the sounds together to make a whole word. Try not to refer to the letters by their names. Help your child to focus on the sounds.
Sometimes your child might bring home a picture book that they know well. Please don’t say, ‘This is too easy.’ Instead, encourage your child to tell you the story aloud; ask them questions about things that happen or what they think about some of the characters in the story.
Reading to your child has a huge impact on your child’s success at school as well as encouraging them to develop a love of reading. Research has proved that reading for pleasure has a powerful impact on children’s cognitive development.
We know parents and carers are very busy people. But if you can find time to read to your child as much as possible, it helps them to learn about books and stories. They also learn new words and what they mean. Show that you are interested in reading yourself and talk about reading as a family.
Does it matter if my child misses a lesson or two?
It matters a lot if your child misses school. The way we teach children to read is very well organised, so even one missed lesson means that your child has not learnt something that they need to know to be a good reader.
What if he or she finds it difficult to learn to read?
We want children to learn to read, however long it takes us to teach them. We will find out very quickly if your child is finding reading difficult. First, we move children to a different group, so that we can make sure that they have learnt what they need to know. If they still struggle, we give them extra time with an adult, on their own. These adults are specially trained to support these children.
If we have any serious worries about your child’s reading, we will talk to you about this.
What if my child turns out to be dyslexic?
The way we teach reading is especially helpful for children who might be dyslexic. This is because we use a very well-organised program that has a strong focus on phonics. This is very important for children who find learning to read difficult. If you are worried about your child, please come and talk to us.
What books will my children bring home to read?
All children also have access to three library areas in school to choose books. They choose books from their class book boxes, their year group library, and they also have a weekly library session in the main School Library. These three books are brought home with reading diaries in each child’s book bag. Reception will start bringing home library books later in the year.
We expect each child to share their books at home each day and for this to be recorded in their reading diary. Please see below for our Home School Reading Policy for reading and phonics at Springfield Infant School.
Home School Reading Policy Download (pdf)

pageCache.pageTitle: Running Club - Springfield Infant School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
Running Club
The running club is open to Year 2 pupils.
The session is held on a Monday during lunchtime and takes place on St Andrews playing field with Oscar from Brighton & Hove Albion. Lunch is taken after the run!
The running club is a great opportunity for children to get fit and have fun while introducing them to the sport of running.
Children will need a full change of clothes to include tracksuit bottoms, trainers, socks and a sweatshirt.
If you have a Year 2 child who is interested in joining this club, please contact the School Office.
